gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Shokz's PC wireless adapter works only with its communication-series headsets (OpenComm/OpenMeet), so the OpenRun Pro 2 cannot use it. None says the OpenComm2 UC's adapter comes as a USB-A or a USB-C version that you pick by your computer's port, or that a non-UC OpenComm2 (2025) can be paired by hand with a Loop120 adapter sold separately for $39.95, which comes to $199.90, about the price of the $199.95 UC bundle.
standout_why: I opened openearclub.com's 'Best Bone Conduction Headphones With Mic' (a top result). It says only 'USB adapter included (UC)' with a '98 ft range' and gives neither the connector type nor which headsets the adapter works with. The RTINGS pages (the cited OpenComm2 2025 review, the cited OpenComm2 2025 vs OpenRun Pro 2 compare, and the OpenMeet UC review) and the Tom's Guide guide came back as navigation shells with no body text. So I could not confirm whether they mention the adapter's limits. I scored this 2 rather than 3 because those cited RTINGS pages are unchecked.
decides: This confirms the split ChatGPT made, with a hard rule behind it: anyone who takes calls on a computer and wants the dongle connection should buy an OpenComm-series headset, because the OpenRun Pro 2 can only use the computer's own Bluetooth. UC buyers need to order the adapter version that matches their port: USB-A for Windows/USB-A machines, USB-C for Macs/USB-C machines. A buyer who isn't sure they need the dongle can get the $159.95 OpenComm2 (2025) and add a $39.95 Loop120 later for about the price of the UC. iPhone users should know that Shokz's OpenComm2 2025 support page says the Shokz App works only on Android phones. The headset itself still pairs with iPhone.

findings.label: Which headsets the adapter works with
findings.value: Shokz communication-series headsets only: 'Loop120 is compatible with all OpenComm series products' and 'only Shokz communication series headsets are compatible with the Loop120 wireless adapter'
findings.note: Quoted from Shokz's US support FAQ. The same page says Loop120 cannot be used for firmware updates to OpenComm headsets through Shokz Connect. The OpenRun Pro 2 support page (separate finding) does not mention any adapter.

findings.label: Adapter connector version to order
findings.value: 'Windows and USB-A computers require the USB-A version, while Macs and USB-C computers need the USB-C version.'
findings.note: Shokz FAQ. The UC ships with its adapter already paired. The same page says the headset pairs with up to two mobile devices at once over Bluetooth.

findings.label: Changes from the original OpenComm2 UC
findings.value: Charging moved to USB-C, the wireless adapter was upgraded, and software control features were added
findings.note: Shokz describes the main change as 'the shift to USB-C charging'. The original OpenComm2 used a magnetic charging cable, so buyers should check which generation a third-party listing is selling.

findings.label: Pairing with the adapter (non-UC)
findings.value: 'OpenComm2 2025 Upgrade requires manual pairing with the Loop120 adapter'; the UC comes with the adapter already paired

findings.label: Exclusions and app platform
findings.value: 'It will not pair with gaming consoles and selet [sic] transmitters'; app features are 'only supported on the Shokz app for Android phones'; pairs with 'most Bluetooth devices that use Bluetooth 3.1 or higher'
findings.note: Shokz FAQ, quoted as written. The page also says the headset works with both iPhone and Android phones; only the app is limited to Android. Multipoint is listed as an app feature without a device count. When both paired devices are in range, the headset prefers the one used most recently.

findings.label: Computer connection and charging
findings.value: Pairs with a PC over the computer's own Bluetooth ('select "OpenRun Pro 2 by Shokz"'); single USB-C charging port; no wireless adapter mentioned
findings.note: Shokz FAQ. The page also says the headphones work without the Shokz App and that the 'Classic' EQ mode turns off the air-conduction driver.
